content.text:
The sync server now uses undici's `fetch` everywhere. I haven't confirmed this fixes the SimpleFIN report, and nothing is committed. The sync-server tests pass (764/764) and lint is clean. `yarn typecheck` fails on one error: `html-to-image` can't be found in `ReportTopbar.tsx`, which is in `desktop-client`, not in anything I changed.

**Likely cause:** SimpleFIN is the only code that passes a `dispatcher` to `fetch`. That dispatcher is an `Agent` from the installed `undici@8.12.3`, but the call was to Node's built-in global `fetch`, which bundles its own, different undici version. Mixing the two is fragile, and the SSRF guard in `util/ssrf.ts` depends on that dispatcher, so a Node or undici version change can break the sync. This is my best guess. I haven't reproduced the user's failure.

**Where the fetch calls were** (all under `packages/sync-server/src`):
- `app-simplefin/app-simplefin.js` has two calls, the claim `POST` and the redirect-following accounts `GET`. Both pass the dispatcher.
- `app-cors-proxy.js` has two calls, the plugin allowlist and the proxy request.
- `app-enablebanking/services/enablebanking-service.ts` and `app-gocardless/services/gocardless-api.ts` have one call each.
- `scripts/health-check.ts` has one call.

Each file now has `import { fetch } from 'undici'`, and I didn't change any other source logic. In `enablebanking-service.ts` I also import undici's `RequestInit` and `Response` types so they match.

**Tests:** they were stubbing `global.fetch`, which no longer affects the code, so I changed them to mock `undici`'s `fetch` instead. That touched seven test files across SimpleFIN, the CORS proxy, Enable Banking and sensitive-logging.

**Environment:** the default shell here uses Node 18, which can't run Vitest. I ran everything on Node 22.20 from nvm, and the server requires Node 22 or newer. If the user reporting the problem is on an older Node, that could also explain the breakage.

I didn't add a release-notes entry. If this repo needs one, I can add it.

content.text:
Port clashes aren't a worry. A server that never answers makes the test fail after Vitest's default 5 seconds, not hang. I made one small hardening change to the test teardown.

**Port clashes:** the test binds with `server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1')`. Port 0 asks the OS for a free ephemeral port, and the test reads the real port back from `server.address()`. The port is never hard-coded, so a taken port can't cause a collision. Binding to 127.0.0.1 also avoids IPv6 and `localhost` resolution problems on odd CI networking. The test doesn't touch DNS, because the address is a literal IP.

**Server that never answers:** `app-simplefin.js` sets no request timeout of its own, and undici's default header timeout is 300 seconds. What bounds the test is Vitest's default 5-second test timeout. To check, I ran a temporary copy of the test whose server accepted requests and never replied. Both tests failed with "Test timed out in 5000ms", and the whole run took about 12 seconds including startup. I deleted that copy afterwards.

**Teardown change:** `server.close()` waits for open connections, so a stalled request could have left `afterAll` hanging. I added `server.closeAllConnections()` before it in `integration.test.ts`. The two real tests pass and lint is clean.

I could add an explicit shorter timeout to the tests, but 5 seconds already seems quick enough. The sync server itself still has no timeout on SimpleFIN requests, so a bridge that never replies would keep a user's sync waiting for up to 300 seconds. The other providers set their own timeouts; for example, Enable Banking uses an abort controller. That isn't part of this bug, but say if you want me to add a timeout to the SimpleFIN calls.

The release-note placeholder is untouched.

content.text:
I'd leave them different, but I'd also drop the sync-server bump back to `>=22`, because I can't find a reason for the higher floor.

**Why different floors are normal here:** the root `package.json` describes what developers need to work on the whole monorepo. Each package's `engines` describes what a consumer of that published package needs. The two don't have to match. `packages/api` and `packages/cli` both say `>=22`, so the sync-server was in line with them until my edit.

**The floor is probably over-strict:**
- The code runs on Node 22.19.0 or newer without trouble, but I haven't found anything that needs it. The undici change works on any Node 22, because it uses the installed `undici@8.12.3` package, not Node's built-in one.
- I bumped it because you remembered 22.19.0 as the floor. I never checked that against the repo.
- A stricter floor makes `yarn install` warn or fail for anyone on 22.0–22.18. That includes self-hosters who run the sync server from npm, and the SimpleFIN user may be one of them.
- The Docker image and CI use Node 24 (`.nvmrc` says v24.22.1), so neither depends on this field.

**What I'd do:**
- If there's a real reason for 22.19.0, such as a dependency's own `engines` or a known Node bug, keep it and raise the root floor to match, since the root should be at least as high as any package.
- If not, revert the sync-server line to `>=22` so this bug fix doesn't add a new requirement.

I lean toward reverting. Do you remember where the 22.19.0 number came from? If a particular dependency or Node bug is behind it, keep the bump. If it was just a feeling, I'd revert.

message.content: Hmm, no, I do think 22.19.0 is the right floor for the sync server, I'm fairly sure that's what we settled on, so please keep it at >=22.19.0 and don't revert it. Sorry I can't point at the exact reason offhand. Leave the root one alone then, different floors are fine. Thanks for the thorough answer, I think we're pretty much done here. Can you commit it? content.text:
The cors proxy tests did not reset the fetch mock between cases. I've now added a reset, and the file passes (36 tests) with lint clean. The fix is not committed yet.

**What was wrong:**
- Before my change the file never cleared the mock globally either. It only called `mockClear()` in three tests.
- It got a fresh call history in other places by accident: several tests did `global.fetch = createFetchMock(...)`, which swapped in a brand-new `vi.fn()` and discarded earlier calls.
- My migration made `createFetchMock` call `mockImplementation` on the one shared `fetch` mock, and that doesn't clear recorded calls. So history could pile up across tests, and a `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` check could pass because of a call from a different test.

**The fix:** the top-level `beforeEach` in `app-cors-proxy.test.js` now calls `fetch.mockClear()`. It clears recorded calls before every test but keeps the implementation, so the shared setup and the per-test overrides work as before.

I didn't check whether any assertion actually passed because of leftover calls. The reset just rules it out.

I haven't amended `567f1496`. Do you want it as a separate small commit or folded into that one?
